bib.title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation

legacy_report:
SOURCE: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation. Fangyuan Xu, Weijia Shi, Eunsol Choi. arXiv:2310.04408v1, preprint (6 Oct 2023). Later published at ICLR 2024, but that is not printed in this PDF.
COVERAGE: 80290 of 80290 chars read. Main text, appendices A.1/A.2, Tables 5-12 and the pseudocode figures were read. The reference list and the long qualitative example tables (6, 7, 9, 11, 12) were skimmed only. Figure images were not viewed. The note (05-chunking-query-parsing-and-reranking.md) does not cite RECOMP. It covers rerankers (bi-encoder, cross-encoder, ColBERT) and the claim that fewer, better chunks cut cost.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Compressing 5 retrieved docs to about 5% of the tokens costs only a few EM points on NQ and TQA.
 number: NQ -2 EM at 5% tokens, TQA -3.7 EM at 5% tokens. Table 2 lists NQ at 36 vs 660 tokens (EM 37.04 vs 39.39) and TQA at 32 vs 677 tokens (EM 58.68 vs 62.37).
 setup: Flan-UL2 20B as the LM, contriever-msmarco retriever, Wikipedia Dec 2018 in 100-word passages, top 5 docs, 5-shot prompt, trained abstractive compressor (T5-large 775M).
 quote: "On NQ, it achieves a compression ratio of 5% tokens while losing 2 EM points compared to prepending full documents. On TQA, we observe similar trends, compression ratio of 5% tokens while losing 3.7 EM points"
 where: p.7, Table 2

2. On HotpotQA (multi-hop) the extractive compressor works better than the abstractive one, and the gain is smaller.
 number: 11% of tokens, -2.4 EM. Table 2: extractive 75 tok, EM 30.40 vs top-5 684 tok, EM 32.80. Abstractive EM is 28.20.
 setup: Flan-UL2, 500 sampled HotpotQA dev examples, extractive selects 2 sentences.
 quote: "we find extractive approach to be more helpful, achieving 11% compression rate while losing 2.4 EM points compared to prepending full documents."
 where: p.7-8

3. Selective augmentation: the abstractive compressor outputs an empty string when retrieval would not help, and is trained to do so by a critic.
 number: 33% of language-modeling examples get a non-empty summary. 4-24% of abstractive training examples have an empty target; Table 5 gives 25% NQ, 16% TQA, 4% HotpotQA, 24% Wikitext.
 setup: A teacher (gpt-3.5-turbo) writes summaries. An example is kept only if the end-task score with the summary beats the score with no retrieval; otherwise the target is empty.
 quote: "Our abstractive compressor achieves high compression rate through selective augmentation, prepending summaries to only 33% of examples"
 where: p.7 and p.8; Fig 3 and Fig 7 pseudocode; Table 5 (A.1)

4. More retrieved text is not always better, and irrelevant documents hurt.
 number: Language modeling, GPT2 PPL: top 1 doc 32.90 (141 tok), top 5 docs 35.53 (512 tok), no retrieval 37.84. QA does gain from 5 docs over 1: NQ EM 39.39 vs 33.07.
 setup: WikiText-103, GPT2 117M, BM25 retrieval every 32 tokens, 100-word docs.
 quote: "More tokens are not always better: prepending top 1 document outperforms prepending top 5 documents."
 where: p.6, Table 1

5. A trained 110M sentence-level extractive compressor beats off-the-shelf rankers.
 number: NQ EM 36.57 (37 tok) vs Contriever 30.06, DPR 34.32, BM25 25.82, Random 23.27. Top-1 doc is 33.07 at 132 tok. TQA EM 58.99 vs DPR 56.58. HotpotQA EM 30.40 vs Contriever 28.60. The extractive oracle reaches NQ EM 60.22.
 setup: Dual encoder initialised from contriever (110M), contrastive loss. Positives are the sentence with the best LM log-likelihood or EM. Negatives are the top 5 Contriever-ranked sentences scoring lower. Top 20 sentences from the top 5 docs.
 quote: "Ours 37 36.57 44.22 38 58.99 65.26 75 30.40 40.14"
 where: p.7, Table 2; p.3-4

6. Off-the-shelf DPR on one sentence beats the top-1 document in-domain, but it degrades out of domain.
 number: 39 vs 132 tokens on NQ.
 quote: "On NQ, selecting the top 1 DPR ranked sentences from top 5 documents outperforms prepending top 1 document, with much fewer tokens (39 vs. 132)."
 where: p.7

7. The language-modeling compressors reach about 25% compression with a small drop vs the top-1 document, and they transfer to larger LMs.
 number: Ours extractive PPL 33.67 / 18.19 / 10.73 at 31 tok. Ours abstractive PPL 33.64 / 18.09 / 10.66 at 15 tok. Top-1 doc is 32.90 / 17.86 / 10.57 (the GPT2-XL token count printed in the extraction, "14", looks like an extraction fault). Oracles use 6-13% of tokens and reach PPL 30.36.
 setup: Compressors trained with GPT2; tested on GPT2, GPT2-XL (1.5B) and GPT-J (6B).
 quote: "Ours (init. w/ T5) 15 33.64 15 18.09 15 10.66"
 where: p.6, Table 1

8. Transfer to another QA LM is weaker.
 number: On LLaMA-13B, NQ EM is 34.38 (extractive) and 36.32 (abstractive), vs 37.04 for full top-5 and 30.89 with no retrieval. The authors say the compressors get 5% compression with under 5 EM drop on NQ/TQA, but not always better than baselines (Contriever vs ours on TQA/HotpotQA).
 quote: "Ours (init. w/ Contriever) 37 34.38 44.15 38 65.28 71.85 75 33.20 42.88"
 where: Table 10, p.21; discussion p.8

9. Naive heuristic compression (bag of words, named entities) is poor.
 number: NQ EM 23.60 (NE) and 28.48 (BoW), vs 21.99 with no retrieval.
 quote: "Top 5 documents (NE) 338 23.60 31.02 128 54.96 61.19 157 22.20 31.89"
 where: Table 2

10. Off-the-shelf T5 gives extreme compression and a small gain, but trained compression is much better.
 number: T5 adds 7-10 tokens for a 4-6 EM gain.
 quote: "Off-the-shelf summarization model (T5) boasts the highest level of compression, achieving 4-6 points gains in EM while adding mere 7-10 tokens."
 where: p.7

11. Models copy from distractors. Compression reduces the wrong-copy rate.
 number: Wrong-copy rate when the gold answer is absent from the evidence: 51% for top-1 doc, 81% for top-5, 85% for GPT-3.5 summaries, 39% for the trained compressor.
 setup: NQ dev; Table 3.
 quote: "Prepending top 5 documents has a higher frequency (81%) of copying incorrectly compared to top 1 document (51%), and GPT-3 compression leads to an even higher incorrect copying frequency (85%)"
 where: p.8-9

12. Abstractive summaries are less faithful than the teacher's, and multi-hop is worst.
 number: Manual check of 30 non-empty summaries per dataset, % useful (faithful and comprehensive): NQ GPT-3.5 83 vs ours 80; TQA 83 vs 77; HotpotQA 50 vs 40. Faithful (Yes): HQA 74 vs 67; NQ 90 vs 80.
 setup: Authors labelled the summaries themselves.
 quote: "NQ GPT-3.5 90 0 10 97 0 3 83Ours 80 13 7 100 0 0 80"
 where: p.9, Table 4

13. Evidence ordering: documents are concatenated in ascending retrieval score, so the best one sits next to the question. Other setup details: the prompt uses 5 random in-context examples with no docs. The compressor is far smaller than the LM (110M extractive, 775M abstractive vs 20B).
 quote: "we concatenate them in ascending order of retrieval score, with the highest scored document closest to the question"
 where: p.5

LIMITS
- Authors concede abstractive compression for multi-hop tasks "demands further study". The extractive compressor is not adaptive: it fixes the number of sentences (1 for Wikitext and NQ/TQA, 2 for HotpotQA) and has no selective augmentation, which they leave to future work.
- The compressor is trained per dataset and per base LM. Transfer to LLaMA-13B is only partial.
- Faithfulness is not trained for. It is checked manually by the authors on 30 samples per dataset.
- Retriever quality was assumed fixed ("Improving retriever is not the focus"). Only one retriever setup, Wikipedia 100-word passages and Flan-UL2 or GPT2-family LMs were tested.
- Oracle numbers are upper bounds that use the gold answer.
- Dated: 2023 models. Teacher is gpt-3.5-turbo. LMs are Flan-UL2, GPT2, GPT-J and LLaMA-13B, all short-context, so conclusions may not hold for modern long-context LLMs.
- Training the compressors requires scoring with the target LM. The paper does not report this training cost.

BUILDS ON: Ram et al. 2023 (in-context RALM; a cross-encoder document reranker, called "similar set-up but less compute efficient"); Shi et al. 2023b (REPLUG); Izacard et al. 2021 (Contriever); Karpukhin et al. 2020 (DPR, contrastive loss); West et al. 2022 (symbolic knowledge distillation with a critic); Jung et al. 2023; Liu et al. 2023 (lost in the middle); Shi et al. 2023a (distraction by irrelevant context); Si et al. 2022; Mallen et al. 2022; Xu & Lapata 2020 (query-focused summarization); Chen et al. 2023 (faithfulness and comprehensiveness labels); Wingate et al. 2022, Chevalier et al. 2023 and Mu et al. 2023 (soft-prompt compression, contrasted); Raffel et al. 2020 (T5).

CODE: Pseudocode only.
- Fig 6 (p.16, QA extractive): positive p_i = argmax Score(M, y_i, [s_j; x_i]). Negatives are the top 5 sentences by encoder score among those that score lower than p_i. The encoder is fine-tuned contrastively.
- Fig 7 (p.16, QA abstractive): s_i = Decode(Mt, [p; x_i; D_i]). If Score(M, y_i, [s_i; x_i]) < Score(M, y_i, [x_i]), the target is the empty string.
- Table 8 (p.19), NQ/TQA teacher prompt: "Compress the information in the retrieved documents into a 2-sentence summary that could be used to answer the question: Question: query Retrieved documents: docs Compressed documents:"
- Training hyperparameters (A.2, p.15): extractive batch 64, lr 2e-5, 1000 warmup steps, 3 epochs. Abstractive batch 16, lr 1e-5, 3 epochs. Teacher temperature 0.7.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): the retrieve, compress, prepend pipeline. One example shows 749 tokens for full docs vs 58 tokens with RECOMP, and both give 2015. Quick overview of the idea.
- Fig 2 and 3 (p.3-4): training algorithms for the extractive compressor and for the abstractive compressor with its critic.
- Fig 4 and 8: histogram of abstractive summary lengths. The wide spread, including empty summaries, is the evidence for selective augmentation.
- Fig 5: data distribution on NQ, TriviaQA and HotpotQA dev sets, in the appendix. Its caption was not read in full.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. The Table 1 token count for GPT2-XL top-1 doc ("14") looks like a typo or extraction fault (it should be about 141). The extraction also garbled Table 5 headers and some Table 10 cells: abstractive oracle NQ F1 "84.87" looks wrong, since EM is 45.60, and the extractive TQA oracle F1 80.46 is below its EM 84.61. Treat those cells as unreliable. Figures were not rendered. The run did not use scripts/papers/figures.py.
